_about: License classification table. Keys are lowercase SPDX ids or Hugging Face license slugs. A value is a class name, or an object overriding class, commercial_use and note. Sources: SPDX license list (spdx.org/licenses), choosealicense.com, Hugging Face license slugs. Informational only, not legal advice. Add or correct entries as needed.

permissive.label: permissive
permissive.note: Permissive: you can use it commercially, modify it, and keep your own code private. Usually you only need to keep the copyright notice.

weak_copyleft.label: weak copyleft
weak_copyleft.note: Weak copyleft: commercial use is fine, but changes to this project's own files must be shared under the same license. Your separate code can usually stay private.

strong_copyleft.label: strong copyleft
strong_copyleft.note: Strong copyleft: commercial use is allowed, but if you distribute software that includes it, the combined work generally must be released under the same license.

network_copyleft.label: network copyleft
network_copyleft.note: Network copyleft: like strong copyleft, and it also applies when you offer the software to users over a network (SaaS). Often a problem for commercial products.

restricted_or_unknown.label: restricted or unclear
restricted_or_unknown.note: Unclear or restricted: this license may limit commercial use or add special conditions. Read it before relying on the project.

sspl-1.0.note: Server Side Public License: not an OSI-approved open source license. If you offer the software as a service you must release your whole service stack under it. Usually unsuitable for commercial products.
